newsitem.title: USA: Guidant gets FDA approval for catheter.
newsitem.headline: Guidant gets FDA approval for catheter.

text.p: Guidant Corp said Friday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) gave it approval to market its newest coronary dilatation catheter, the ACS Tx2000(TM).

The catheter, manufactured by Advanced Cardiovascular Systems Inc, which is part of Guidant's Vascular Intervention group, is used to open blocked arteries during percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA).

Guidant said the ACS Tx2000 catheter offers extended pressure balloon material, allowing the doctor greater flexibility of inflation strategies, while its slender design and low crossing profiles provide easy access to cross and open the blockage.

"The introduction of the ACS Tx2000 provides physicians with new options to tailor catheter needs to individual patients," Ginger Howard, president of the Vascular Intervention group, said in a statement.
The ACS Tx2000 has been approved and available outside the United States since July 1996. Marketing of this catheter in the United States will begin immediately.
